subject.title: [Feature]: Configurable auto-cleanup and archival policy for webhook/hook sessions

question: Should OpenClaw add an explicit hook-session cleanup policy, and what default mode and transcript-retention semantics should it use alongside session.maintenance, cron cleanup, and persistent hook-session reuse?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but choosing on-complete versus delayed cleanup, whether transcripts are deleted or archived, and how cleanup interacts with persistent hook sessions is a product and data-retention decision automation should not make.

options.title: Add Explicit Hook Cleanup Policy
options.body: Introduce a default-safe hooks.sessionCleanup style policy with on-complete, delayed, and never modes plus transcript-retention behavior and focused hook/session tests.

options.title: Rely On Generic Session Maintenance
options.body: Document that hook sessions are governed only by session.maintenance age/count/disk controls and close hook-specific cleanup as not planned.

options.title: Defer Until Persistent Mode Settles
options.body: Pause this policy until https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/11665 and its persistent hook-session API are accepted or rejected.

recommendation.title: Add Explicit Hook Cleanup Policy
recommendation.body: Introduce a default-safe hooks.sessionCleanup style policy with on-complete, delayed, and never modes plus transcript-retention behavior and focused hook/session tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter already framed this issue as a product/API decision and has the strongest discussion plus path-history routing signal.
